P1.evidence: Setter notes referenced but not read back, same pattern as every call in this batch — 'I spoke to Kim. You had a call with him some time ago. So he briefed me on your situation... but I'm kind of an old school guy and I'm old. So I would like to hear directly from you.' No frame of any kind was set — not the four parts, not three, none — and no agreement was asked for. The open question ran cleanly: 'walk me through what's actually been going on with your fitness right now. And what's the main thing that you're looking to change?'

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline in the batch. Sleep was worked properly for once — 'When you go to sleep, usually what time is it? And you wake up at?', then quality, then 'What are you taking for sleep?', then 'when you wake up, are you feeling groggy?' Injuries were probed for pattern and frequency, not just listed: 'When does that appear during the day? Because you also mentioned some muscle stiffness. Is that connected to each other?' and 'Is it like every single day?' Training week, results and diet all ran. Age came from the setter's notes rather than being asked ('you're 28, as I remember'), height was volunteered, weight was never established, occupation was confirmed from notes rather than asked, and no health-conditions question was put at all — only injuries.

P3.evidence: Best goals work in the batch. P3a was specific and physical: 'which parts of your body doesn't feel still like you want to be?' produced chest, stomach, love handles. The bridge ran explicitly — 'what's your biggest why for doing this? Like, deeper why, you know?' — and produced discipline and self-proof rather than aesthetics. P3e ran as a future-pace: 'if we're sitting six months from now... it actually worked for you... So what does that feel like for you?' P3g landed on identity: 'that version of you, like, let's say Nikhil 2.0, how does he carry himself differently? Like, not just physically, but like in general?' And the reflect-back was genuinely good: 'this isn't an effort issue, because you're clearly disciplined. You show up, but effort alone stops creating results, because you've hit the ceiling of what you can do alone.' The gap is P3f — 'who else does that impact' was never asked, so the why stayed entirely self-contained with no one else in it.

P4.evidence: The plateau was established well — 'have you actually been getting closer to where you want to be physically, or has it been more like...' produced 'pretty much treading water', and 'how long would you say that has that felt like stalled?' produced 'that's been pretty much the whole time I've been working out'. But the root-cause chain was not worked. The February-to-May collapse surfaced and was never probed ('I barely worked out. I was extremely busy with work and I just, it, my path and I just lost it there for a bit'). Prior PTs were volunteered, not asked about. The single biggest miss is P4e: the rep named the gap himself — 'you've hit the ceiling of what you can do alone with the same routine' — which is an accurate diagnosis and exactly the move the script says to hand to the prospect. Letting Nikhil arrive at it would have been worth more at the close.

P5.evidence: The only real consequence frame in this batch, and it worked. P5a ran properly framed: 'if nothing structurally changes, like, not in a doom and gloom way, but just, like, practically, like, where does that trajectory goes over next two to five years if nothing changes?' P5b then ran twice, and the second time with real pressure — 'Because at the end of the day, I thought I heard that that would be acceptable for you, but I was like, okay, so why are we here?' — which forced 'No, no, no, no, not at it wouldn't be. It wouldn't be acceptable at all.' The 'why not' was answered by the prospect volunteering his brother as proof of concept rather than being asked. No line in the sand was ever requested.

P6.evidence: P6b ran cleanly and, crucially, before the price: 'if we can figure out all the details, like the logistics, are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work to become that 2.0 version of Nikhil?' answered 'For sure, for sure.' P6c is satisfied — a clear yes was in hand before the investment was walked through, and the price then landed with no resistance at all. P6a is only partial because what was checked was approach fit ('Does this approach feel like it would actually work for you?') rather than belief that he can get there with the right structure and person in his corner.

P11.evidence: Step one failed and steps three and four never happened. No payment was collected — the link went out, the prospect said 'I can't just pay for it right now', and the rep accepted a deferral to end of day and then to a 9am call the next morning. The onboarding call with Trevor was booked, which is the only completed step, but it was booked with zero collected and against the manager's explicit 06/22 instruction that Trevor's calendar must not carry an unpaid booking: 'So I'm booking the call with Trevor either way.' The agreement was referenced ('you're going to be signing also an agreement') but never sent, confirmed or signed on the call. The welcome email, the Skool community link and the onboarding questionnaire were never mentioned.

objection_plays.detail: The trigger is textbook fear and doubt: 'you see things on Instagram all the time, right? And it's like paying without trying' and 'when you pay for something, you obviously want to try it.' The rep ran credibility hard — six years, over 1,000 clients, a guarantee on paper with a signed agreement — which is adjacent to the play but is not the play. None of the scripted moves ran: no 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty', no pleasure-versus-pain question, no bridge frame, no plane metaphor, no burned-before frame, and critically not 'how will you know if you never actually try', which was the exact objection in front of him. The doubt was resolved by selling him a trial rather than by handling it.

The trigger is real but not a capacity one — 'I can't just pay for it right now... my money is in both places, because it's in dollars... Mainly my money's in pounds.' None of the play ran. No isolate, no SHOULD-versus-HOW, no permission question, none of the six financial-picture questions. More to the point, the rep did not attempt the obvious commercial answer either: no card, no partial payment, no attempt to establish what was accessible right now. He simply accepted 'till the end of the day' and rebooked. Against a prospect who had just said yes to $6,000 without blinking, that is a soft handling of the only thing standing between the call and collected cash.

Script gap, and now a repeating one. The prospect asked to meet the coach before paying — 'it'd be good to meet Trevor before I make a significant, you know, investment' — a reasonable request from a qualified buyer, and there is no play for it. The answer given was a bare process assertion plus a challenge question, 'So the process is that it's always after after payment. Why would you ask?', which is the deflection pattern coached in the 06/26 meeting and which reads as defensive against a trust objection. The 06/29 team meeting shows the identical refusal given to a different prospect the same week, and in both cases it was resolved by improvising a price rather than by any scripted move. This gap is costing the team money and credibility and should go to the playbook, not to the reps.

notes: Phases 2, 3, 5 and 6 are the best work in this batch — the sleep and injury probing, the deep why, the two-to-five-year frame and a commitment check taken before the price. Then P11 collapsed: no payment, no agreement, no welcome steps, and Trevor's onboarding call booked against an unpaid deal in direct breach of the stated rule. Two coaching points. First, when a prospect who has just accepted the price says he needs to move funds, work the payment on the call — find what is accessible now — instead of rebooking. Second, when someone asks to meet the coach, that is a trust objection, and answering it with 'why would you ask' and then a discount trains him to negotiate rather than to trust.
